subject: Kemi
title: Atoms and elements
sourceSummary: The atom as the building block of everything, the difference between an element and a chemical compound, chemical symbols for common elements, what a molecule is and how the periodic table is arranged.
topics: the atom as a building block

questions.topic: the atom as a building block
questions.opener: Think about the smallest piece you can divide an element into while still having the same substance left.
choices: The smallest drop you can divide a liquid into
The smallest building block that an element is made of
A mixture of several different substances
Another name for a water molecule
questions.explanation: The atom is the smallest building block in an element - everything around you is built from atoms. A drop of water is not remotely the smallest possible amount; it contains an unimaginable number of billions of atoms.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for the element oxygen?
questions.opener: The symbol comes from the Latin name oxygenium, not from the English word.
choices: S
Sy
C
O
questions.explanation: Oxygen has the chemical symbol O, from the Latin oxygenium. S is the symbol for sulphur and C for carbon - so you cannot guess the symbol from the first letter of the English name.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an element?
questions.opener: An element consists of only a single kind of atom.
choices: Iron (Fe)
Water (H₂O)
Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
Table salt (NaCl)
questions.explanation: Iron contains only iron atoms and is therefore an element. Water, carbon dioxide and table salt are chemical compounds - you can see this in the formulas, which contain more than one chemical symbol.

questions.prompt: How are the elements arranged in the periodic table?
questions.opener: The number shown next to each element is called the atomic number.
choices: By how large the atoms are
By atomic number, meaning the number of protons in the nucleus
In alphabetical order of their English names
By how much the substances cost to buy
questions.explanation: The elements are arranged in order of atomic number, which is the number of protons in the nucleus: hydrogen is number 1, helium 2, lithium 3 and so on. They are not in alphabetical order - you can see that straight away, since hydrogen (H) comes first and not some element beginning with A.

questions.prompt: In the formula H₂O there is a small 2 after the H. What does it mean?
questions.opener: The number tells you how many atoms of that particular kind are in the molecule.
choices: That there are two water molecules
That the hydrogen has a charge of 2
That the molecule contains two hydrogen atoms
That the oxygen weighs twice as much as the hydrogen
questions.explanation: The 2 shows the number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule: a water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. If you want to show two whole molecules, you instead write the number in front of the formula, i.e. 2 H₂O.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol Cu?
questions.opener: The symbol comes from the Latin name cuprum - think of a reddish-brown colour.
choices: Carbon
Calcium
Chlorine
Copper
questions.explanation: Cu is the symbol for copper, from the Latin cuprum. Carbon has the symbol C, calcium Ca and chlorine Cl - all of these begin with C in English, which is exactly why you have to learn the symbols rather than guess them.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide has the formula CO₂. Use the formula to explain why carbon dioxide is a chemical compound and not an element, and work out how many atoms a carbon dioxide molecule consists of.
questions.opener: Read the formula symbol by symbol: which kinds of atoms are present, and how many of each?
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound because the molecule contains two different kinds of atoms (carbon and oxygen), and each molecule consists of 3 atoms in total: 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms.
steps: Break the formula down into its chemical symbols: C stands for carbon and O stands for oxygen.
Read off the numbers: there is no number after C, which means 1 carbon atom. After O there is a 2, so there are 2 oxygen atoms.
Count the total number of atoms: 1 + 2 = 3 atoms in each carbon dioxide molecule.

Draw the conclusion: since the molecule contains two DIFFERENT kinds of atoms joined together, carbon dioxide is a chemical compound. An element, such as oxygen gas O₂, contains only one kind of atom.

questions.prompt: Summarise the key atomic concepts and the chemical symbols you need to know by heart.
questions.opener: Take the concepts atom, element, molecule and compound first, then the symbols.
questions.answer: Atom: the smallest building block in an element, everything is built from atoms · Element: only one kind of atom, e.g. iron (Fe), oxygen gas (O₂) · Chemical compound: at least two different kinds of atoms bonded together, e.g. water (H₂O), carbon dioxide (CO₂), table salt (NaCl) · Molecule: two or more atoms joined together, can be of the same kind (O₂) or different kinds (H₂O) · Chemical formula: the symbols show which atoms are present, the small number after a symbol shows how many of that atom there are · Chemical symbols: H = hydrogen, O = oxygen, C = carbon, N = nitrogen, Fe = iron (ferrum), Cu = copper (cuprum), Na = sodium, Cl = chlorine, S = sulphur · Capital letter first, lower-case letter second: Co is cobalt but CO is carbon monoxide · Periodic table: all known elements arranged by atomic number (the number of protons), metals to the left and lower down, non-metals to the upper right, the noble gases furthest to the right.
